questions.q: Fix for report register: 'We organized a great event and everyone loved it.'
questions.a: 'The event drew participation from 12 schools' — passivized, quantified, no 'we'. A wrong answer keeping 'we organized' shows the institutional-vs-personal stance confusion.

questions.q: Which lead is board-grade: 'On 5 August, the school hosted its annual blood donation camp in the auditorium, where 120 donors participated' or 'It was a proud day when we all gathered for a noble cause'?
questions.a: The first — compressed 4W + scale. The second is a narrative opening performing pride instead of reporting facts.

questions.q: A report reads 'the principal was very happy' — what improves it?
questions.a: Convert to an attributed quote — 'The participation was heartening, said the Principal' — certification through quotation beats adjective-assertion.

questions.q: Class 12 reports add precision: the lead compresses What/When/Where/Who in ~25 words; body paragraphs deploy passive ______ for objectivity ('the prizes were distributed'); and quotes must carry attribution.

Fill in the blank: Class 12 reports add precision: the lead compresses What/When/Where/Who in ~25 words; body paragraphs deploy passive ______ for objectivity ('the prizes were distributed'); and quotes must carry attribution.
Fill in the blank: ______ mechanics: passive voice removes the reporter — 'the winners were felicitated' not 'we felicitated the winners'.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student writes a board-standard report with compressed lead, passive-voice objectivity, attributed quotes, and correct length — no narrative or opinion drift.
